CHAPTER III.
A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale


On the bank, the soaked creatures debated how to get dry. The Mouse
suggested a Caucus-race: everyone ran in a circle, starting and
stopping whenever they liked, until the Dodo declared "Everybody has
won, and all must have prizes." Alice handed out comfits from her
pocket as prizes, and received a thimble of her own as a prize in
return.

The Mouse began to tell its long and sad tale, but grew offended
when Alice seemed inattentive, and stalked off before finishing.
Left alone, Alice thought sadly of her cat Dinah, which had scared
away all the other animals.
